traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Pennantiaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire or dentate; veins pinnate; stipules absent; plants hermaphrodite, dioecious or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody; flowers solitary, in cymes or in panicles; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually sepals and petals, rarely tepals; fruit drupe; parts of each whorl 5; stamens 5; carpels 2 to 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
